title: ReVeraSchema
description: Re-Vera shared contract — the single source of truth for the backend and every client. Generated into backend/app/schema_models.py (Pydantic v2) and extension/src/types/schema.ts (TypeScript) by shared/generate.sh. This root object exists only so that every type in $defs is reachable from the root; nothing sends or receives it.

Verdict.title: Verdict
Verdict.description: The only four verdicts Re-Vera may produce. Display names are sentence case: Supported, Contradicted, Missing context, Unverifiable. Never TRUE/FALSE, never all-caps, never alternative vocabulary such as "flagged".

Confidence.title: Confidence
Confidence.description: Three-level confidence, never a percentage. Rendered as a three-dot meter. Null (see Claim.confidence) if and only if the verdict is "unverifiable", in which case the UI hides the meter entirely.

Stance.title: Stance
Stance.description: How a retrieved source relates to the claim it was retrieved for.

CheckRequest.title: CheckRequest
CheckRequest.description: Body of POST /check. The extracted article text plus the anonymous install ID. Article text is cached by URL hash, never by user; never log the text alongside install_id.

url.description: Canonical URL of the article being checked. The cache key is sha256 of this string.

title.description: Article headline as extracted from the page.

text.description: Full extracted article body as plain text. Claim.start and Claim.end are character offsets into this string.

install_id.description: Anonymous per-install UUID from chrome.storage.local. Used only for the daily cap.

CheckJob.title: CheckJob
CheckJob.description: Response to POST /check. The client then opens GET /check/{job_id}/stream.

cached.description: True when the result came from the 7-day URL cache and the stream will replay everything immediately.

claim_count.description: Number of claims, known up front only on a cache hit; null on a cache miss.

Source.title: Source
Source.description: One piece of retrieved evidence behind a claim.

date.description: Publication date as an ISO 8601 calendar date, e.g. "2026-03-12".

wire.description: True when this is wire copy; near-identical wire text across domains counts as one source.

TrailNode.title: TrailNode
TrailNode.description: One step of the provenance trail, e.g. label "Original source", note "gov.sg press release, 12 Mar".

label.description: Node title, e.g. "This article", "Independent reports", "Original source".

note.description: Muted detail line for the node.

Claim.title: Claim
Claim.description: One checked claim. Payload of the SSE "claim" event and the unit stored in the cache.

id.description: Stable id within the job, e.g. "c1".

quote.description: Exact substring of CheckRequest.text — text[start:end] must equal this.

start.description: Character offset of the quote's first character in CheckRequest.text.

end.description: Character offset one past the quote's last character in CheckRequest.text.

confidence.description: Null if and only if verdict is "unverifiable".

evidence.description: One plain-language sentence naming the sources. For an "unverifiable" verdict it explains what was searched and not found.

sources.description: Empty if and only if verdict is "unverifiable".

Counts.title: Counts
Counts.description: Per-verdict tally for the finished article.

ClaimsFoundEvent.title: ClaimsFoundEvent
ClaimsFoundEvent.description: First SSE event of a job: how many claims will be checked, and which ids they are, in article order. A client allocates one row per id up front and fills each row when its "claim" arrives, so the live stream (which resolves out of article order) and a cache replay (which does not) render identically, and every row is written exactly once.

count.description: Number of "claim" events that will follow. Always equal to claim_ids.length.

claim_ids.description: Every Claim.id this job will send, in article order (ascending by the claim's start offset). Row n belongs to claim_ids[n], whatever order the claim events arrive in.

DoneEvent.title: DoneEvent
DoneEvent.description: Final SSE event of a successful job. The stream closes after this.

checked_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the check finished.

ErrorEvent.title: ErrorEvent
ErrorEvent.description: Terminal SSE event when a job fails. The stream closes after this.
